blocking.item: B1. The unit cannot be fitted into the r2 tray. Affects: lid_tray_qmx_r2.py lines 151-152 (the lintel at each end), the fitting step (sheet 14r2-2 note 2, the section E1 caption), the draft's ASSEMBLY step 10 and tray row, SC-64 'taken', and the closing of S-63.
blocking.problem:
The lintel at the keeper end covers x -50.5 to -47.5, runs the full width (y +-35.8) and sits at z 27.1 to 29.1, which is the height of the unit's top face. The only documented way in is to slide the unit in from the keeper end, right panel first, under both ledges and that lintel. Everything that stands above the top face must pass under it. With the pads fully squashed the gap is 0.50 mm.

What stands above the top face:
- The two encoder shafts, with or without their knobs. The maker's assembly manual 1.04r page 77, photographs 13 and 15, shows the shafts and the knobs, which are held by grub screws.
- The two push-button actuators (6x6x8 mm switches), which photograph 15 shows standing about 2 mm above the face. They cannot be removed.

Checker's boolean test on the box (build123d 0.13.0, the author's module sha 3e89a3ca), sweeping each item from outside the keeper end to its seated place against build_tray():
- unit body alone: 0.000 mm3
- 15 mm knob, 11.6 high: 90.000 mm3 each
- bare 6 mm shaft, 5 mm high: 36.000 mm3 each
- button 3.5 mm, only 0.6 high: 1.050 mm3 each

lid_tray_qmx_r2_check.py tests only the seated position, so its PASS says nothing about fitting. As drawn, the tray cannot take an assembled QMX, and S-63 (the tray does not fit the unit) cannot close on it.

Fix: remove the keeper-end lintel, or move it onto the removable keeper so it is screwed on after the unit is in. Then add a swept-insertion check that uses the maker's top-face items (encoder shafts, knobs, button actuators) and a control case that must collide. Scripts: scratchpad/chk-w5tray/insertion_check.py.

blocking.item: B2. The face-room limits in lid-tray-qmx-r2-check.out section B are wrong: rows M3r2b and M3r2k. The same figures are carried into the r2 README, sheet 14r2-1, the drafted S-82 title, the CASE-FIT-UNCERTAINTIES row and ASSEMBLY step 11.
blocking.problem:
(a) M3r2b is wrong by 2.0 mm. It measures the C&K buttons from the unit's top face (29.30 from the ceiling) and reports 'MET for caps up to 11.81, 14.09 at the worst'. But each of SW_MAIN (150,60), SW_PI (150,10) and SW_TEST (150,-33) sits under a tray element 31.30 deep:
- SW_MAIN and SW_TEST under the end lintels
- all three under the back ledge (case X 155.0 to 159.0)

The record itself prints the buttons' column as X 140.4 to 159.6, which overlaps that ledge. The checker's solid check (deepest tray point over each plate-hole footprint) gives z 29.10 for all three, so the correct limit is caps up to 9.81 with unstated allowances taken twice, and 12.09 at the plain worst. After apply_frame_seat_r2.py, frame_seat.py's M3 row uses 31.30 and so contradicts M3r2b.

(b) The 'unstated x2' column says it takes every unstated allowance twice, but it leaves out the r2 stack's own allowances:
- the printed ledge height, which the record uses elsewhere as PRINT_TOL 0.2 in section C and which sets the unit's top face
- the unstated thickness tolerance of the 2.0 mm 5052 plate

With PRINT_TOL taken twice alone, the inferred 11.6 knob's 1.21 mm falls to 0.81, below the 1.0 minimum. M3r2k is therefore OPEN, not 'MET on the INFERRED knob', and 'MET for a knob up to 11.81' is too generous by at least 0.4 mm. The verdicts stay OPEN, but the stated limits are wrong and would wrongly pass a later reading of a cap or knob height.

Fix: compute every row with the deepest element over each item's footprint and the stack's own tolerances. Script: scratchpad/chk-w5tray/buttons_under.py.
